added: #Find the circuit breaker box. Some homes will have multiple breaker boxes in different places. Find both the main circuit breaker box and the one you need to replace a circuit breaker in.<ref>http://www.visionaware.org/info/everyday-living/home-repairs/gils-guide-to-home-repairs/fuses-and-circuit-breakers/1235</ref> If you’re unsure about the circuit breaker boxes in your home, call an electrician.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 1 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Inspect the exterior of the breaker panel for damage or discoloration. Before you begin working on any breaker boxes, you should make sure they are still in a safe condition. Any damage or contamination to the box may make it unsafe to work on.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 2 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Use rubber-insulated tools, gloves, and shoes. Electricity can be incredibly dangerous to work around, so take all precautions when trying to reduce the chance of an electrical shock.<ref>https://www.ehs.washington.edu/fire-life/basic-electrical-safety</ref> Use rubber insulated tools, and wear rubber-soled shoes and insulated gloves when working with electricity.<ref>https://youtu.be/k95_Rnjr_DY?t=41s</ref>[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 3 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Locate the defective breaker. You should only replace a circuit breaker that has broken or been damaged in some way. If a circuit breaker is damaged, it will likely have tripped, cutting power to the section of the home it controls. Look through your breaker box for the circuit breaker which stands out from the others. Generally, a tripped circuit breaker switch will be halfway between the on and off positions.<ref>https://brightnest.com/todos/fix-a-blown-fuse-or-reset-a-circuit-breaker</ref>[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 4 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Test the faulty breaker. Before you replace a circuit breaker, make sure the breaker itself is faulty and not just overloaded. Unplug and switch off all light and electrical devices in the section of your home controlled by the circuit breaker. Then, turn the breaker switch completely off and back on again. Plug one device back in to see if it is powered to indicate if the breaker is allowing any power through or if it is completely broken.<ref>https://brightnest.com/todos/fix-a-blown-fuse-or-reset-a-circuit-breaker</ref>[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 5 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Test the voltage of the circuit breaker. If you want to test the circuit breaker more specifically, you can do so with a voltage tester. To do so, unscrew and remove the faceplate, and press one lead to the neutral wire in the breaker box. Press the other lead to the screw on the circuit breaker. The voltage tester should display how much power is being allowed through the breaker.<ref>https://youtu.be/jKAPpxK5T2E?t=21s</ref>[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 6 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Turn off all power and all individual breakers. Before doing any work on a circuit breaker or in the breaker box, make sure you have turned off all the power going to it. If you have a main box and other branch boxes around your home, turn off the power to the branch box at the main box first. Otherwise, just turn off the main power followed by all breakers.<ref>https://youtu.be/jKAPpxK5T2E?t=1m31s</ref>[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 7 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Unscrew and remove the faceplate. While the circuit breaker box will allow you to switch breakers on and off, this will not give you access to the entire circuit breaker. Find the screws in each corner of the breaker box and carefully remove them to free the faceplate. Holding the edges, lift the faceplate directly away from the breaker box before lowering it.<ref>https://youtu.be/k95_Rnjr_DY?t=1m</ref>[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 8 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Inspect the interior of the panel for damage or discoloration. Before you touch anything inside the panel of the breaker box, look for signs of damage. If you see anything that seems unsafe or out of the ordinary, stop immediately and call a licensed electrician.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 9 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Pull out the faulty breaker. When touching items inside the circuit breaker box, always be careful to only touch the components you need to. With a firm grip, grasp the defective circuit breaker. Start lifting the side that faces towards the center of the panel, with the aim of pivoting it up and out from the breaker panel. Once it is free, unhook it from the hinge on the edge of the panel and pull the breaker free.<ref>https://youtu.be/jKAPpxK5T2E?t=2m31s</ref>[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 10 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Disconnect the wire on the circuit breaker. The wire connected to the circuit breaker will be held in by a flathead screw on one side. Use a flat-head screwdriver to loosen this screw slightly, without unscrewing and removing it completely. Separate the wire from the circuit breaker once the screw is loose enough.<ref>https://youtu.be/jKAPpxK5T2E?t=2m42s</ref>[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 11 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Note the exact amperage and type of the circuit breaker. The circuit breaker replacement will need to be the exact same type as the faulty one you remove.<ref>https://youtu.be/zqcJFfWYiAI?t=33s</ref> Take note of the amperage of the fault breaker, as well as any codes or numbers written elsewhere on it.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 12 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Dispose of the faulty circuit breaker. While a circuit breaker may feel heavy, there is very little value to any of its components.<ref>http://trustwaymetal.com/can-you-scrap-circuit-breakers/</ref> You can throw circuit breakers away with your regular trash, as they are inert without a power supply.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 13 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Find a new circuit breaker of the same type as the faulty one. The new circuit breaker will need to be exactly the same type as the one you are replacing.<ref>https://youtu.be/zqcJFfWYiAI?t=33s</ref> Your local hardware store should have a selection of circuit breakers and may have the exact one you are looking for. If not, feel free to ask the staff if they can get one in for you, or if there is one you may have missed.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 14 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Clip the new circuit breaker in place. Using the opposite motion to removing the faulty breaker, firmly clip your new circuit breaker into place. Position the end without a screw under the hook on the breaker box panel, and pivot the breaker down until it clicks into place securely.<ref>https://youtu.be/jKAPpxK5T2E?t=3m37s</ref>[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 15 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Reattach the loose wire. Firmly hold your circuit breaker and connect the wire to the loose screw.<ref>https://youtu.be/k95_Rnjr_DY?t=2m37s</ref> Keeping it in place, tighten the screw until it securely holds the wire.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 16.jpg|center]]

#Reattach the faceplate. Carefully lift the faceplate in line with the breaker box and install it back in place. Using the same screws that came out of the faceplate, tightly secure the faceplate to the rest of the breaker box.<ref>https://youtu.be/jKAPpxK5T2E?t=4m35s</ref>[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 17.jpg|center]]

#Turn the power back on. If you have a main breaker box, turn on the power to your branch breaker box first. Turn on the main power in the breaker box, followed by each circuit breaker one by one.<ref>https://youtu.be/jKAPpxK5T2E?t=4m45s</ref> You should start getting power back to your home.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 18.jpg|center]]

added: A circuit breaker is designed to stop the power flow through a circuit if there is an excessive amperage drawn on said circuit. Occasionally, these breakers go bad and will need to be changed. It is highly recommended that you hire a licensed, competent, and insured electrician to perform this task, as electricity can be deadly. However, if you choose to replace a circuit breaker yourself, you’ll need to know how to find the breaker box, take note of any issues, and replace a faulty breaker to get your power working again.
==Steps==
===Investigating the Faulty Circuit Breaker===

#Find the circuit breaker box. Some homes will have multiple breaker boxes in different places. Find both the main circuit breaker box and the one you need to replace a circuit breaker in.<ref>http://www.visionaware.org/info/everyday-living/home-repairs/gils-guide-to-home-repairs/fuses-and-circuit-breakers/1235</ref> If you’re unsure about the circuit breaker boxes in your house, call an electrician.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 1.jpg|center]]

#Inspect the exterior of the breaker panel. Before you begin working on any breaker boxes, you should make sure they are still in a safe condition. Any damage or contamination to the box may make it unsafe to work on.

#*Look for any signs of rust, discolouration, charring or moisture when you first examine the circuit breaker box and throughout the process. If you see anything that seems dangerous or unexpected, call an electrician.

#*Beware of certain types of panels, specifically those bearing one of the following names: Federal Pacific Electric, Federal Pioneer, Zinsco, Kearney, GTE Sylvania, or Stab-lok. The safety of these panels is highly debated.<ref>https://www.angieslist.com/articles/what-are-signs-home-electrical-problems.htm</ref> Research the issue, and contact an experienced electrician for advise. Decide what to do based upon the information you find.

#Take the appropriate safety precautions. Electricity can be incredibly dangerous to work around, so take all precautions when trying to reduce the chance of an electrical shock.<ref>https://www.ehs.washington.edu/fire-life/basic-electrical-safety</ref> Use rubber insulated tools, and wear rubber-soled shoes and insulated gloves when working with electricity.<ref>https://youtu.be/k95_Rnjr_DY?t=41s</ref>

#*If you don’t have rubber-soled shoes or if you want to take further precautions, put down a rubber mat below the circuit breaker box. If the area around the breaker box is damp or otherwise unsafe, call an electrician.

#Locate the defective breaker. A tripped breaker switch will be halfway between the on and off positions. Look for the circuit breaker that stands out from the others in your breaker box.<ref>https://brightnest.com/todos/fix-a-blown-fuse-or-reset-a-circuit-breaker</ref> [[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 2.jpg|center]]

Press one lead to the neutral wire in the breaker box, and one to the screw on the breaker to test the voltage.<ref>https://youtu.be/jKAPpxK5T2E?t=21s</ref>

#*If you think the breaker is tripping without being overloaded, it may be wearing out and have a reduced capacity for amperage. If you think this is the case, you should [[Determine Amperage of Circuit Breaker|check the amperage of your circuit breaker]].

#Turn off all power and all individual breakers. Before doing any work on a circuit breaker or in the breaker box, make sure you have turned off all the power going to it. #*Always keep track of loose wires, as they can be incredibly dangerous. You will also need to know which wire to attach to your new circuit breaker.

#Note the exact amperage and type of the circuit breaker. The circuit breaker replacement will need to be the exact same type as the faulty one you remove.<ref>https://www.angieslist.com/articles/what-are-signs-home-electrical-problems.htm</ref> Take note of the amperage of the fault breaker, as well as any codes or numbers written elsewhere on it.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 7.jpg|center]]

#Dispose of the faulty circuit breaker. While a circuit breaker may feel heavy, there is very little value to any of its components.<ref>http://trustwaymetal.com/can-you-scrap-circuit-breakers/</ref> You can throw circuit breakers away with your regular trash, as they are inert without a power supply.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 10.jpg|center]]
===Installing a New Circuit Breaker===

#Find a new circuit breaker. The new circuit breaker will need to be exactly the same type as the one you are replacing.<ref>https://www.angieslist.com/articles/what-are-signs-home-electrical-problems.htm</ref> Your local hardware store should have a selection of circuit breakers and may have the exact one you are looking for. If not, feel free to ask the staff if they can get one in for you, or if there is one you may have missed.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 11.jpg|center]]

#Clip the new circuit breaker in place. Using the opposite motion to removing the faulty breaker, firmly clip your new circuit breaker into place. Position the end without a screw under the hook on the breaker box panel, and pivot the breaker down until it clicks into place securely.<ref>https://youtu.be/jKAPpxK5T2E?t=3m37s</ref>

#Reattach the loose wire. Firmly hold your circuit breaker and connect the wire to the loose screw.<ref>https://youtu.be/k95_Rnjr_DY?t=2m37s</ref> Keeping it in place, tighten the screw until it securely holds the wire.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 12.jpg|center]]
#*It may help to use a pair of needle nose pliers to hold the wire in place as you tighten the screw.<ref>https://youtu.be/k95_Rnjr_DY?t=2m28s</ref>

#Turn the power back on. If you have a main breaker box, turn on the power to your branch breaker box first. Turn on the main power in the breaker box, followed by each circuit breaker one by one.<ref>https://youtu.be/jKAPpxK5T2E?t=4m45s</ref> You should start getting power back to your home.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 15.jpg|center]]

== Steps ==
# Find the main circuit breaker box. Some homes may have 1 large main breaker box as well as smaller branch breaker boxes.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 1.jpg|center]]
# Locate the defective breaker. A tripped breaker is halfway between the on and off position.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 2.jpg|center]]
#* Before assuming a circuit breaker needs to be replaced, try resetting the breaker by turning off all lights and unplugging all devices on that circuit. Then turn the back to the on position.
#* Some breakers must be turned all the way off before they can be turned back on.
#* Test the circuit breaker by turning on the breaker, and then add the devices 1 at a time. If the light or device becomes operable, then a voltage tester is not needed.
# Use a voltage tester to see if power is going out through the wire attached to the breaker.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 3.jpg|center]]
# Turn off the branch breaker boxes, followed by the main power.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 4.jpg|center]]

#* This should be the large flip switch located above or below all the other smaller ones. It should also be labeled "main" or something similar. The main breaker typically has the largest amperage rating of all the breakers in the panel.
# Turn off the individual breakers.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 5.jpg|center]]
# Inspect the exterior of the panel. If there is evidence of rust, charring, discoloration, moisture, or other contamination, DO NOT proceed, and call an electrician immediately.

# Beware of certain types of panels, specifically those bearing one of the following names: Federal Pacific Electric, Federal Pioneer, Zinsco, Kearney, GTE Sylvania, or Stab-lok. The safety of these panels is highly debated. Research the issue, and contact an experienced electrician for advise. Decide what to do based upon the information you find.
# Use protective equipment. Wear insulated lineman's gloves and use insulated lineman's tools. Wear rubber-soled shoes and safety glasses, and stand on a rubber mat.

# Be sure the area around you is safe. If there is water or another liquid present, do not proceed. Call a licensed electrician immediately. Also, be sure that there is plenty of clearance above, below, to the sides of, and in front of the panel.

# Remove the screws holding the face plate (called a "dead front") with a Philips screwdriver. Use the left hand rule when opening the panel to prevent injury in the event of an arc flash. [[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 6.jpg|center]]
# Read the label on the main power switch to determine what kind of circuit breaker box you own.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 7.jpg|center]]

# Inspect (without touching anything) the interior of the panel. Look for signs of rust, moisture intrusion, pest intrusion, loose wires, melting, discoloration, charring, heat marking, multiple wires under one screw, aluminum wiring, wiring with damaged insulation, knob and tube wiring, strange modifications, debris, and multiple colored wires connected to each other. If ANY of these conditions are found, or if another type of strange thing is found, do not proceed. Call a licensed, competent, and insured electrician.
# Loosen the screws that hold the wires found on the defective breaker.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 8.jpg|center]]
# Remove the breaker from the panel.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 9.jpg|center]]
# Discard the old circuit breaker.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 10.jpg|center]]

# Replace the old circuit breaker with the new one. The replacement breaker must have the same amperage and be the same type (unless using "classified" breakers) as the previous breaker. Snap the circuit breaker back into the same place as the old on the panel.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 11.jpg|center]]
# Place the wires in the new circuit breaker as they were in the old one.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 12.jpg|center]]
# Tighten the screws. Do not over tighten, but do not leave too loose either.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 13.jpg|center]]

# Replace the circuit panel's faceplate. If any of the original screws were lost, replace them with FLAT-ENDED MACHINE SCREWS. Using pointed wood screws may damage wiring inside the panel.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 14.jpg|center]]
# Turn on the main power, followed by the individual breakers.[[Image:Change a Circuit Breaker Step 15.jpg|center]]
*Do not replace a circuit breaker with one of larger amperage. This may cause a dangerous wiring overload.

added: A circuit breaker is connected to an electrical circuit and is designed to stop the power flow though the circuit in the event there is a surge, arc, or short. Occasionally, however, these breakers go bad, and you will need to know how to change a circuit breaker. Follow the steps to learn how to replace a circuit breaker.
== Steps ==
# Find the main circuit breaker box. Some homes may have 1 large main breaker box as well as smaller branch breaker boxes.
# Locate the defective breaker. A tripped breaker is halfway between the on and off position.
#* Before assuming a circuit breaker needs to be replaced, try resetting the breaker by turning off all lights and unplugging all devices on that circuit. Then turn the back to the on position.
#* Some breakers must be turned all the way off before they can be turned back on.
#* Test the circuit breaker by turning on the breaker, and then add the devices 1 at a time.
# Use a voltage tester to see if power is going out through the wire attached to the breaker.
# Turn off the branch breaker boxes, followed by the main power.

#* This should be the large flip switch located above or below all the other smaller ones. The smaller circuit breakers will have small numbers on them from 10 to 60, while the main power breaker will have numbers such as 100, 150, or 200.
# Turn off the individual breakers.
# Remove the screws holding the faceplate with a Philips screwdriver.
# Read the label on the main power switch to determine what kind of circuit breaker box you own.
# Loosen the screws that hold the wires found on the defective breaker.
# Remove the breaker from the panel.
# Discard the old circuit breaker.

# Replace the old circuit breaker with the new one. The replacement breaker must have the same amperage and be the same type as the main breaker. Snap the circuit breaker back into the same place as the old on the panel.
# Place the wires in the new circuit breaker as they were in the old one.
# Tighten the screws. Do not over tighten.
# Replace the circuit panel's faceplate.
# Turn on the main power, followed by the individual breakers.
== Tips ==
* If the circuit breaker you are replacing is a GFI breaker, as sometimes used for kitchen or bathroom circuits, be sure that you replace it with another one.
* You may need someone to hold a flashlight while you change out a circuit breaker. Many breaker boxes are located in dark areas such as basements and closets.
== Warnings ==
* If you cannot find the main power cut off switch, do not attempt to remove a circuit breaker or work on the circuit panel. Contact an electrician.
* Do not replace a circuit breaker with one of larger amperage. This may cause a dangerous wiring overload.
== Things You'll Need ==
* Voltage tester
* Philips screwdriver
* Replacement circuit breaker
* Flashlight
